questions.question: A parser misses a new phrasing of a purchase. Which fix holds up better over many filings?
options: Add the new phrasing to a word list
Raise whenever holdings change and no parsed purchase explains it
Skip releases the parser does not understand
Estimate the purchase from the holdings change
questions.explanation: Build note #16: three review rounds of word lists kept finding new phrasings. A structural guard fails loudly on any unexplained change, whatever the wording.

questions.question: Two share counts are available. One matches Strategy's API more closely but cannot be traced to a filing. Which one does the project use?
options: The closer one
The average of the two
The one that traces to a filing
Neither; it anchors to the API
questions.explanation: Build note #14 and decision R7: every input must trace to a filing. The error rose from 0.02% to 0.11%, still inside the 0.5% gate.

questions.question: BitMine's stated ETH change equals "ETH acquired" in 13 of 16 weeks. What does that imply for a separate staking carry row?
options: It is needed to make attribution sum
It should be booked only in the other 3 weeks
It has no effect on the ETH check
It counts staking twice, since "acquired" already includes it
questions.explanation: With staking rows the ETH site check read +0.52% (a fail); without them, -0.0006%. The decision was reversed after looking at the data (#15, #6).

questions.question: The 2026-08-23 residual was $1,570.1M with a disclosure row for USD Cash. What does 2,006.5 - 136.4 - 300.0 = 1,570.1 show?
options: The USD Cash came from that week's MSTR sale proceeds, already booked by issue_common, so the disclosure row counted it twice
The USD Cash existed before 8/23
STRC retirements were missing
The reserve rounding was too tight
questions.explanation: The 8-K filed 2026-08-24 funds USD Cash from the remaining MSTR sale proceeds. Removing the row dropped the residual from 37.9% to about 0.5% (#19).

questions.question: A step in a GitHub Actions job hangs past the job's timeout-minutes. What happens to the alert step that has if: failure()?
options: It runs, because the job failed
It runs twice
It is skipped, because GitHub cancels the job rather than failing it
It opens a new issue per day
questions.explanation: Build note #20: a job timeout cancels the job. A step-level timeout inside the job fails only that step, so the alert still runs.
